problem: Generic reward models are built for static inputs or simple outcomes and cannot evaluate embodied question answering (EQA) trajectories, which depend on spatial grounding, temporal ordering and reasoning coherence. EQA evaluation also has no benchmark for reward models, and existing ones only score final-answer correctness.
motivation: Reward models supply the signals for aligning and selecting agent behavior. EQA agents need fine-grained feedback on their reasoning and grounding, not only on the final answer. The authors observe that SFT alone mostly teaches output style, so they add a contrastive RL stage that forces the RM to notice perturbed temporal, spatial and logical context.
key_idea: Train a generative multimodal reward model (critique + score) with RFT followed by Contrastive GRPO, which rewards more accurate scoring on original inputs than on temporally shuffled, spatially masked or reasoning-jumbled inputs, and then scale its evaluation at test time by sampling K critiques and aggregating.
insight: Test-time scaling delivers most of the gain: accuracy rises from 42.47 to 61.86 (K=32) overall, whereas the untrained Qwen2-VL-2B shows no positive accuracy trend with K. In the ablation, RFT alone (31.69) and RL without RFT both stay at or below the base model (33.08), so RFT cold-start is needed. The contrastive rewards then lift accuracy only after RFT, and the reasoning reward gives the largest single gain (+9.32). Note that the full four-term reward (42.47) is barely better than R_r alone (42.40) or R_s+R_r (42.44), so the perturbation rewards mainly help RMSE and combinations rather than accuracy.
method: EQARewardBench construction: built on OpenEQA. Gemini-2.0-Flash generates diverse correct and incorrect answers with reasoning traces. Gemini-2.5-Pro, given the ground-truth answer, produces a critique and a 0-10 score, with human verification, and these scores serve as s_gt.
Data split: 1,536 test instances (823 HM3D, 713 ScanNet) form the benchmark; the other 697 ScanNet instances are held out for fine-tuning. Evaluation is ScanNet ID and HM3D OOD.

Rejective Fine-Tuning: an auxiliary evaluator without GT answer samples N candidate critique+score pairs per instance. Candidates within tolerance τ of s_gt are kept, and instances where all candidates are correct (too easy) are dropped. Qwen2-VL-2B is SFT'd on the rest with NLL loss to learn the format.

C-GRPO perturbations: temporally shuffled frames, spatially masked frames (16x16 patches, ratio 0.15), and jumbled reasoning-trace steps. The RM scores original and perturbed versions of each instance.

Rewards: accuracy reward max(0, 1-(|s_r-s_gt|/10)^2), format reward, and a contrastive boost μ=0.3 for each augmentation x whenever the batch-mean original accuracy reward ≥ δ·(batch-mean x-augmented reward), δ=0.95. Total reward is R_a+R_f+(R^t+R^s+R^r)/3.
GRPO update: group-normalized advantages over G=8 generations, PPO-style clipping, KL coefficient 0.04; 5 keyframes per episode, lr 1e-6, one epoch.
Test-time scaling: sample K∈{1,...,32} critique-score paths at temperature 0.8 and top-p 0.9, then aggregate by majority voting or by averaging scores.

setting.training_data: 697 ScanNet OpenEQA-derived instances (question, answer, reasoning trace, video, Gemini-2.5-Pro GT score); RFT candidates from an auxiliary LLM evaluator
setting.observation: 5 keyframes from the episode-memory video, plus question, predicted answer and reasoning trace
setting.action_space: not applicable (text output: critique and 0-10 scalar score)
setting.simulator: none (offline OpenEQA video data from HM3D and ScanNet)
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT scores come from Gemini-2.5-Pro with the GT answer, used only for training and benchmark labels)

numbers.extra: K=32 sampled critiques aggregated; tolerance τ=2 accuracy
numbers.evidence: Table 1 (Main evaluation results on EQARewardBench), w/ test scaling (K=32) row

numbers_note: Benchmark is the paper's own EQARewardBench (reward model accuracy), not a navigation benchmark. Split marked 'test' as the paper names no official split. The text says 61.9% in one place and 61.84% in the conclusion; Table 1 gives 61.86. The abstract says 'only 700 samples'; the training set is 697 instances. Test-time scaling curves are given in a figure only.
results: With K=32 test-time scaling, EQA-RM (Qwen2-VL-2B) reaches 61.86% overall accuracy and RMSE 2.727. This beats Gemini-2.5-Flash (59.79), GPT-4o (58.45), Claude-3.5-Haiku (56.00), RoVRM (39.18) and VisualPRM (38.74), and it has the best RMSE. Without scaling it reaches 42.47%, below the proprietary judges but with lower RMSE.
limitations: Contrastive augmentations are predefined (shuffle, mask, jumble) and may miss other failure modes; the ablation shows the spatial reward hurts on its own.
Ground-truth scores come from Gemini-2.5-Pro with the GT answer, so its biases propagate into training and evaluation; generalization beyond OpenEQA is untested.
Evaluated only as an offline scorer; downstream use for policy improvement and critique faithfulness were not studied, and K=32 sampling is costly.
